patch: 0783-perf-dsv41-extend-WO-B-WIDE_DECODE-to-128-rows-and-g.patch (the WO-B part: gemm.py, wo.py and their test, split at selection)
mark: WO-B part only. Its WO-B bench (mxfp8_gemm and TileLangWOProjection at M=104..128, K=3072/2048/1024) on the image, 2 boots, ABBA: faster beyond the interval at M=97..128, torch.equal against the prefill GEMM; the engine grid's 16-stream cell not worse. It acts only at TP4: rows past 96 need 16 streams with copy widening (107 rows at max_num_seqs 16; TP3's 8 streams reach 59)

arms.base: spark-ds41f:candidate-50 sha256:8c1ea1f62f62c3e2adc03b645c091a5499cf7163101aca32875c894b96f155db + candidate-50 no1009/overlay (4 files, ro): tree 14c5a2dc; WIDE_DECODE[(5120, K)] = {96: 96}
arms.c51: the same image + the 15 files where candidate-51's tree differs (ro): tree 987ba058 (cc1115c5); WIDE_DECODE[(5120, K)] = {96: 96, 128: 128}

bench_written: The PR's /tmp/bench_wo_b.py is not committed at 9be94ed5 (only receipts/wo_b_boot{1,2}.json), so we wrote h987.py (../common/h/h987.py), keeping the PR's workload and claim: WO-B (5120 x K, block-32 FP8 weights from the PDL-chain test helper, MXFP8 activations written by WO-A) at K = 3072 / 2048 / 1024 with WO groups 3 / 2 / 1 (TP3 ranks 0-1 / TP4 and TP3 rank 2 / TP8), and the end-to-end TileLangWOProjection (WO-A + its cast + WO-B), at M = 64, 96 (unchanged tiles) and 97, 104, 107, 112, 120, 128. It calls the image's own kernels through the serving dispatch (linear._block32_gemm on TileLangWOProjection's WO-B, which picks the tile with decode_tile_rows), so one script measures both arms: the base launches 64-row tiles at 97..128, the candidate the 128x128 tile. Bit-exactness: torch.equal against the prefill GEMM (mxfp8_gemm with fp8_prefill_config on the same 128 rows), padding rows poisoned (E4M3 NaN, UE8M0 0xFF) as test_wo_b_wide_decode_128_rows_matches_prefill does, plus output hashes across arms. Timings: CUDA-graph replay L2-hot (20 back-to-back calls a graph, 30 replays) and L2-cold (one call a graph after a 256 MiB write), CUPTI kernel time, eager loop; >= 250 ms GPU warm-up first. h987b.py (boots 3-4) adds CUPTI kernel time with a sync after each call and WO-A alone. The PR's receipts list more tile candidates (decode_128_64x128_s3 etc.); ours times only what each image dispatches.
evidence: Two ABBA pairs in one session (base 1, c51 1, c51 2, base 2; later base 3, c51 3, c51 4, base 4), judged per pair and pooled over four boots. Then the mark's tests on c51.

wob_graph_hot_us_base_to_c51 (boots 1-2).M=64 and 96 (unchanged tiles): same in 5 of 6 cells; K=2048 M=64 faster 1.029x

measured.wob_kernel_back_to_back_cupti (boots 1-2: slower in 16 of 18 cells at 97..128 (e.g. K=2048 M=107 43.08/43.31 -> 50.19/49.50): in a back-to-back loop a PDL kernel's span includes its early-launch wait, and the 40-CTA tile launches earlier; the isolated kernel time above is the kernel's own

e2e_TileLangWOProjection.graph_hot pooled 4 boots: K=3072 6 of 6 faster; K=1024 6 of 6 faster (1.02-1.03x); K=2048 6 of 6 same. K=2048 hot is unstable in both arms (base M=107 75.98/78.92/102.80/75.76, c51 M=97 88.66/77.61/72.26/94.74), while WO-A alone (34-36 us) and WO-B alone are stable
e2e_TileLangWOProjection.graph_hot per pair: K=2048: the first pair reads M=97, 107 and 128 slower (0.918x, 0.917x, 0.936x) and the second pair reads those same but M=120 slower (88.00/91.01 -> 96.81/99.12, 0.914x): the slower cell moves between pairs, and pooled over four boots no cell is slower
e2e_TileLangWOProjection.wo_a_alone (boots 3-4, code #987 does no: graph_hot: no cell slower; graph_cold: 3 slower by 1.6-2.0% (K=2048 M=112, 120, 128); kernel_isolated: 4 slower (K=1024 x3, K=3072 x1): the A/A spread of this two-boot rule

pytest_c51.first runs (pytest-c51-boot1/2): exit 4: tests/conftest.py imports tblib, which the image lacks; kept
pytest_c51.with the release bundle's tblib stand-in: 7 passed on both boots (6.95 s, 7.03 s): test_wo_b_wide_decode_128_rows_matches_prefill[3072, 2048, 1024], test_mxfp8_decode_tile_repeats, and the three tests of test_deepseek_v41_block_scale_words.py

measured.engine_grid_16_stream_cell: not measured here: the screen at tp4-ring (screen-tp4.json) judges it

bit_exact_detail: WO-B's output equals the prefill GEMM's (torch.equal, padding rows poisoned) in every cell of all eight runs, on both arms, and so does the end-to-end projection's; the output hashes are equal across all eight runs in every cell (the 64-row and the 128-row tiles give the same bits).
reason: Bit-identical to the prefill GEMM, the 128-row WO-B tile is faster beyond the interval at every M=97..128 cell of all three shapes by CUDA-graph replay, L2-hot and L2-cold (TP4's K=2048: 1.13-1.16x hot, 1.11-1.14x cold, pooled over four boots), and by isolated kernel time (15 of 18 faster, 3 same). The end-to-end TileLangWOProjection is faster L2-cold at all six TP4 cells (1.05-1.07x) and unchanged L2-hot, where its timing is unstable in both arms. No cell at M<=96 is slower over four boots. The end-to-end L2-hot cells at K=2048 that read slower on one ABBA pair (three in the first, a different one in the second) are same over four boots. The mark's engine-grid condition is the screen's to judge.
notes: Measured on spark-ds41f:candidate-50 with candidate-51's tree mounted; the trees are verified file by file (../common/verify).
The c51 arm's gemm.py also carries #963, whose changes are in the packed-BF16 kernels, not the MXFP8 GEMM WO-B runs; wo.py is #987's alone.
At M=97..128, the row counts this acts on at TP4 are 104 and 112 (c16 with CopyDrafter replays the 104- and 112-row graphs); 107 is the widest c16 step.
The CUPTI back-to-back kernel time is recorded but not used: it counts PDL early-launch waits (kernel_isolated is the decider beside graph replay).
start_utc in commands.txt is after the GPU lock was taken; other agents' jobs ran between runs.
